texts: good. the wraith, the draining, the lanterns as one definite set being drained, and the named West Row with its kind are all carried.

bad: two losses. "drained" is dropped entirely, so nothing records that the lanterns are in a drained state, and the per-lantern rule the parse adds hands every single lantern the same handful of nightmoths — claiming each lantern separately attracts the whole handful, which you say only of the lanterns as a set. Rewrite as "The lanterns are drained, and together they attract a handful of nightmoths." — the separate clause gives "drained" somewhere to land, and "together" keeps the attracting collective so the count stays with the group.

bad: "what happens to X" has no question form the translator can build — the harvest is hung off a bare "to" modifier that no statement would ever fill (and which can collide with the purpose "to" of another sentence), so the question asks for an event aimed at the harvest rather than one that befalls it, and it binds nothing. Name the event and make the harvest its object: "What ruins the thread harvest?" — substitute the verb you actually mean (eat, spoil, ruin), so the harvest sits in the object slot an answering sentence would really use.
